name: Browserbase
summary: Browserbase runs real Chrome browsers in the cloud that your own Playwright or Puppeteer code connects to and controls remotely.

free_plan_covers.note: Free plan includes 1 browser hour a month and 3 concurrent browsers, enough for a developer's own testing, not real user traffic.

first_paid_usd_month.note: Developer plan is $20/month for 100 browser hours, then $0.12 for each extra browser hour.

portability.note: Your scraping code is standard Playwright or Puppeteer connecting over CDP, so pointing it at a different browser provider, or your own server, is mostly a matter of changing the connection URL.

scraper_runs.note: You write Playwright or Puppeteer code that connects to a real Chrome browser Browserbase runs for you, instead of sending a URL and getting a finished page back.

js_rendering.note: Sessions are full browsers, so JavaScript-rendered pages just work, billed at the same per-browser-hour rate as any other page.

ai_ready_output.note: Its separate Fetch API can return a page as clean Markdown by passing format: 'markdown', billed apart from browser-hour sessions.

price_per_1k_pages.value: About $4 per 1,000 pages in browser time (roughly 33 browser-hours at the Developer plan's $0.12/hour overage rate), assuming about 2 minutes of browser time per page, which is Browserbase's own estimate that 100 browser hours covers about 3,000 page-level tasks. That pace fits inside the 100 hours already included in the $20/month Developer plan.
price_per_1k_pages.note: Estimate built from Browserbase's own stated ratio of browser hours to page-level tasks, applied to the Developer plan's overage rate.

setup.step: Sign up for a free Browserbase account and copy your API key from the dashboard.
Install the packages with npm install playwright-core @browserbasehq/sdk.
Add your key as BROWSERBASE_API_KEY in your environment file.
In a server route, create a Browserbase session, connect Playwright with chromium.connectOverCDP(session.connectUrl), then drive the page as you normally would.

builder_notes: Keep BROWSERBASE_API_KEY server-side; drive sessions from a route handler, server action, or background job, never from client code.
Always close the browser and session when you're done with it, since an open session keeps burning browser-hour billing.
Respect each target site's robots.txt and terms of service before automating it.
